verdict.summary: Any workspace admin can create a Linear OAuth app, and no Linear review was found before it can authorize users. Set distribution to public and other workspaces can install it. The only review found is optional: the curated Integration Directory listing, which turns away hobbyist and low-effort apps. Customer workspaces on paid plans can also turn on their own admin approval before your app is installed.
verdict.approval_wait: none (Integration Directory listing is optional; no published review timeline)

gates.name: Private app (home workspace)
gates.unlocks: You can connect your own Linear account in the workspace where you created the app.
limits: Distribution is private by default: installable only in the workspace where the app was created
Access tokens expire after 24 hours and need a refresh token; the old refresh token works for a 30-minute grace period
Rate limit is 5,000 requests per hour per user (or app user) and 2,000,000 complexity points per hour

gates.name: Private app shared with workspace members / public app installed by invited workspaces
gates.unlocks: Other members of your home workspace can authorize the private app. With distribution set to public, workspaces you invite can install it too.
limits: Linear documents no tester allowlist and no install or user cap for unreviewed apps
On paid plans, a customer workspace's admin can turn on Third-party application approvals; members must then request approval and wait for that admin
Same 24-hour token expiry and per-user rate limits as Gate 1

gates.name: Public distribution (optional Integration Directory listing)
gates.unlocks: Any Linear workspace can install the app. Listing in Linear's Integration Directory, which is optional, adds discoverability.
limits: No Linear review was found for public installs; this rests on the absence of any mention in the docs
The Integration Directory is curated: it accepts integrations from formal companies that are useful to the community, and generally not scripts, low-effort apps or hobbyist builds
Directory assets: 320x320 colour and monochrome icons and 1-3 showcase images at 1600x1000
Customer workspaces may still require their own admin's approval to install
gates.time_to_reach: Public installs: minutes. Directory listing: unknown, since no timeline is published

steps.title: Pick or create a dedicated Linear workspace where you are admin
steps.detail: Linear recommends managing the OAuth app from its own workspace, because every admin of that workspace gets access to the app. You need to be a workspace admin to create and manage OAuth apps.
gotchas: The app belongs to the workspace, not to you personally. Every admin of that workspace can see and edit it.

steps.title: Open the new OAuth application form
steps.detail: Go to Settings > API, scroll to OAuth Applications, and click Create new OAuth Application. You can also open the new-application URL directly. Community guides also call this section 'Your Applications'.
gotchas: The menu label may change. The direct URL from Linear's docs is the most reliable way in.

steps.title: Fill in the app identity fields
steps.detail: Enter an app name, a developer name and a homepage/docs URL (client_uri). An agent can build a URL that pre-fills the create form, or a JSON manifest, so the setup is easy to repeat.

values.label: Application name
values.value: 2-80 characters; must not contain 'Linear' or an http(s) URL

values.label: Developer URL / homepage (client_uri)
values.value: Your product homepage or docs URL (required)

gotchas: Names containing the word 'Linear' are rejected.
The findings don't say whether the live form also asks for a privacy policy, logo or description.

steps.title: Add the redirect URI
steps.detail: In the callback/redirect URLs field, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. It must be an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL. An app can register 1 to 32 of them.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect_uri in the token exchange must exactly match the one used in the authorize request.

steps.title: Choose distribution and grant types
steps.detail: Leave distribution on private (the default, home workspace only) while testing. Switch it to public when other workspaces need to install the app. authorization_code is always on. Turn on client credentials tokens only if you need app-actor tokens without a user.

values.label: Distribution
values.value: Private for Gates 1-2 testing; Public for Gate 3

gotchas: Client-credentials tokens last 30 days, and up to 1,000 can be active at once if they share scopes.
Rotating the client secret immediately invalidates client-credentials tokens, but not user access or refresh tokens.
A webhook URL, if you set one, must be HTTPS and must not point to a loopback host, a private-network host or linear.app.
One community guide says to enable refresh tokens in the app settings. If you see that toggle, turn it on.

steps.title: Save the app and copy the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Save the app, then copy the Client ID and Client Secret into a Composio Linear auth config that uses your own credentials. Set scopes to the minimum you need, for example read, write, issues:create and comments:create.

values.label: Scopes
values.value: read,write,issues:create,comments:create (comma-separated; add admin only if truly required)

gotchas: Linear's docs say never to request admin unless it is absolutely needed. Check whether your Composio auth config added it by default.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection through Composio, approve the Linear consent screen, and confirm a GraphQL call works. If the flow uses PKCE, it must send code_challenge_method=S256. To act as the app rather than the user, add actor=app.
gotchas: The authorize page renders even with a bad client_id, so an invalid client only fails later in the flow.
Linear publishes no OIDC discovery document. Use the endpoints from the OAuth docs.
Add prompt=consent if one user needs to connect several workspaces.

steps.title: Confirm token refresh works
steps.detail: Access tokens expire after 24 hours. Each refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token, so the stored refresh token must be replaced every time. Treat an invalid_grant refresh error as a cue to ask the user to reconnect.
gotchas: An old refresh token still works for 30 minutes after rotation, but don't rely on it.

steps.title: Share with teammates and invited workspaces
steps.detail: Members of your home workspace can authorize the private app. For other workspaces, set distribution to public and send them your connect link. If a target workspace has Third-party application approvals turned on, its admin must approve the request first.
gotchas: Approval requests go to workspace admins (owners on Enterprise) by email and in-app notification. Admins can deny with a reason.

steps.title: Go public
steps.detail: Set the app's distribution to public so any workspace can install it. The findings show no Linear review step for this.

steps.title: (Optional) Prepare Integration Directory assets
steps.detail: For a listing in Linear's Integration Directory, prepare a 320x320 colour icon and a monochrome icon (.svg, .jpeg or .png), 1-3 showcase images at 1600x1000, and the listing copy.

steps.title: (Optional) Submit to the Integration Directory
steps.detail: Fill out Linear's directory submission form, then email the assets to integrations@linear.app or link to them. Expect rejection if the app is a script, low-effort or a hobbyist build.

steps.title: (Optional) Wait for directory review
steps.detail: Linear publishes no review timeline. Public installs already work while you wait. Send follow-ups and listing changes to integrations@linear.app.

requirements.item: Workspace admin role in the workspace that owns the app
requirements.detail: Only workspace admins can create and manage OAuth apps. Linear recommends a dedicated workspace for the app.

requirements.item: App name, developer name and homepage URL
requirements.detail: client_name: 2-80 characters, without 'Linear' and without a URL. Developer name: 2-80 characters. client_uri is required.
1-32 absolute HTTP or HTTPS URLs. The one used must match exactly in both the authorize and token steps.

requirements.item: PKCE with S256 if using PKCE
requirements.detail: Since October 2026 Linear requires an explicit S256 method. Plain challenges should not be used.
Tokens expire after 24 hours, and refresh tokens rotate on every refresh.
Needed for workspaces other than yours to install the app.
Built by a formal company and useful to the community. Icons and showcase images in the listed sizes. No privacy policy, demo video or security assessment requirement was found.

scopes.effect: Always included. No review tier was found.
General write access. No extra review was found.
Narrower than write: allows creating issues only. No extra review was found.
Allows creating comments only. No extra review was found.
Documented scope. No extra review was found.
No review gate is documented, but Linear says never to request it unless absolutely needed. Users may hesitate to approve it, and customer-workspace admins reviewing approvals may turn it down.
Agent-specific scopes documented in the App authentication docs, which were not reviewed. Check that page before requesting them.

blockers.symptom: No option to create an OAuth application under Settings > API
blockers.cause: You are not a workspace admin
blockers.fix: Ask an admin for the admin role, or create your own dedicated workspace for the app.

blockers.cause: The name contains 'Linear' or a URL, or is outside 2-80 characters
blockers.fix: Rename the app, e.g. 'Acme Agent' rather than 'Acme for Linear'.

blockers.symptom: Redirect or token exchange fails with a redirect_uri mismatch
blockers.cause: The callback URL registered in Linear doesn't match the one Composio sends, or a different URI was used at the token step
blockers.fix: Copy the exact callback URL from the Composio auth config into the app's redirect URIs.

blockers.cause: code_challenge_method is missing or set to plain
The refresh token expired, was revoked or is unknown, often because a rotated refresh token wasn't stored
blockers.fix: Store the new refresh token after every refresh. Ask the user to reconnect when invalid_grant appears.

blockers.symptom: Users in a customer workspace can't finish installing; the request sits pending
blockers.cause: That workspace has Third-party application approvals turned on
blockers.fix: The user's workspace admin (owner on Enterprise) must approve the request under Settings > Administration > Security.

blockers.cause: Over 5,000 requests per hour per user, or over the complexity budget
blockers.fix: Respect the Retry-After header. Ask Linear support for temporarily higher limits if needed.

blockers.cause: The directory turns away scripts, low-effort apps and hobbyist builds
blockers.fix: Public installs work without a listing, so you can distribute without one. Re-apply once the app is a maintained product from a company.

blockers.cause: The URL is not HTTPS, or points to a loopback host, a private-network host or linear.app

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Linear OAuth app. It works right away. Register your own Linear OAuth app when you need your own client credentials or branding on the consent screen, a stable redirect URI, or client-credentials (app-actor) tokens. Setup is self-serve and needs no Linear review. Composio's guide lists 'admin' as a default scope but the toolkit catalog does not, so check your auth config's scopes and remove admin unless you truly need it.

evidence.claim: Linear's OAuth docs say to create an OAuth2 application from the settings link and set its redirect callback URLs.
evidence.quote: Create a new OAuth2 Application and configure the redirect callback URLs to your application.

evidence.claim: Access tokens last 24 hours, refresh tokens rotate on each refresh, and the old refresh token has a 30-minute grace period.
evidence.quote: The access token is valid for 24 hours and will need to be refreshed when it expires.

evidence.claim: All OAuth2 apps were moved to the new refresh token system on 1 April 2026.
evidence.quote: All OAuth2 applications were migrated to the new refresh token system on April 1, 2026.

evidence.claim: Refreshing an expired, revoked or unknown refresh token returns invalid_grant.
evidence.quote: Fixed OAuth token refresh to return invalid_grant for expired, revoked, or unknown refresh tokens

evidence.claim: The code exchange is a form-encoded POST to https://api.linear.app/oauth/token. PKCE flows send code_verifier and can omit client_secret.
evidence.quote: Pass parameters in body as URL-encoded form submission

evidence.claim: Client-credentials tokens must be switched on in the app settings. They last 30 days, and up to 1,000 can be active at once.
evidence.quote: You must first toggle on client credentials tokens for your OAuth2 app when creating or editing the app in Linear

evidence.claim: Rotating the client secret immediately invalidates client-credentials tokens but not user tokens.
evidence.quote: Rotating your client secret immediately invalidates any client credentials tokens issued for your application.

evidence.claim: Documented scopes are read, write, issues:create, comments:create, timeSchedule:write and admin. admin should only be requested when absolutely needed.
evidence.quote: You should never ask for this permission unless it's absolutely needed

evidence.claim: Agent-specific scopes such as app:assignable and app:mentionable are documented in the App authentication section.
evidence.quote: See App authentication for agent-specific scopes such as app:assignable or app:mentionable.

evidence.claim: The OAuth page flags no scope as sensitive, restricted or review-gated. This guide infers there is no scope review tier.
actor=app makes the app the actor for mutations, which suits agents.
evidence.quote: actions performed with the received OAuth token will come from the app itself

evidence.claim: Linear recommends a dedicated workspace for managing the OAuth app, because every admin in that workspace gets access to it.
evidence.quote: It is highly recommended you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application

evidence.claim: prompt=consent forces the consent screen every time, so one user can connect multiple workspaces.
evidence.quote: The consent screen is displayed every time, even if all scopes were previously granted.

evidence.claim: Linear's OAuth page and changelog state no install cap or user limit for unreviewed OAuth apps.
evidence.quote: It is highly recommended you create a workspace

evidence.claim: OAuth apps get 5,000 requests per hour per user (or app user) and 2,000,000 complexity points per hour.
evidence.quote: OAuth App | 5,000 | User (or App User) | 1 hour

evidence.claim: Over-limit requests get a 429 RATELIMITED error. Higher limits can be requested from Linear support.
evidence.quote: If you temporarily require higher limits, you can request them by contacting Linear support

evidence.claim: Third-party app approvals are available on paid plans, and admins turn them on under Settings > Administration > Security.
evidence.quote: Third-party application approvals are available on any paid plan.

evidence.claim: Installing members can request approval, admins are notified, and denials can carry a reason.
evidence.quote: Workspace owners in Enterprise workspaces—and workspace admins in all other paid workspaces—will receive an email

evidence.claim: Linear announced third-party app approvals on paid plans in September 2026.
evidence.quote: Third-party app approvals are now available on paid Linear plans

evidence.claim: A community integration guide says only a workspace admin can create and manage OAuth apps in Linear.
evidence.quote: You must be a workspace admin to create and manage OAuth apps in Linear.

evidence.claim: The Integration Directory generally does not accept scripts, low-effort apps or hobbyist builds.
evidence.quote: We generally do not accept scripts, low-effort/vibe coded or apps built by hobbyists

evidence.claim: Directory submission is a form plus assets sent to integrations@linear.app, including 320x320 icons and 1600x1000 showcase images.
evidence.quote: Color icon 320px by 320px in .svg, .jpeg, or .png file format

evidence.claim: No directory review timeline is given. Listing changes go through integrations@linear.app.
evidence.quote: you can contact integrations@linear.app with the updates required.

evidence.claim: Linear recommends building OAuth apps in a separate workspace.
evidence.quote: We recommend building applications using OAuth and having a separate workspace for the application

evidence.claim: The directory docs list no privacy policy, domain verification, demo video, security assessment or install minimum.
Linear's OIDC discovery URL returns 404.
The authorize endpoint returns HTTP 200 for an invalid client_id, so client validation happens later in the flow.
Distribution is either private (default, one workspace) or public (installable by other workspaces).
evidence.quote: Whether the app should be available only in the current workspace or installable by other workspaces.

evidence.claim: client_name must be 2-80 characters with no 'Linear' and no URL. Developer name and client_uri are required.
evidence.quote: Must not contain `Linear`

evidence.claim: A community guide places the OAuth applications list under the API page in workspace settings.
evidence.quote: Scroll down to OAuth Applications and select Create new OAuth Application.

evidence.claim: authorization_code is always required and client_credentials is optional. Webhook URLs must be HTTPS and not loopback, private-network or linear.app.
evidence.quote: The host must not be a loopback host, private-network host, or `linear.app`

evidence.claim: URL parameters can pre-fill the create form, and a JSON manifest format exists.
evidence.quote: URL parameters for pre-populating the Create OAuth app page

evidence.claim: A third-party guide says admin should be used with caution.
evidence.quote: admin: Full access to admin level endpoints (use with caution)

evidence.claim: A community SDK guide places app creation at Settings > API > Your Applications.
evidence.quote: Settings -> API -> Your Applications

evidence.claim: A community guide says to enable refresh tokens in the OAuth app settings.
evidence.quote: In the OAuth app settings, enable refresh tokens.

evidence.claim: Nothing in Linear's docs suggests a waiting period or review before a new OAuth app can authorize users.
Linear's OAuth docs link directly to the new-application page.
evidence.quote: Create a new OAuth2 Application

evidence.claim: The authorize request requires client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code and a comma-separated scope list. state is recommended, and PKCE is supported.
evidence.quote: Comma separated list of scopes

evidence.claim: Linear requires an explicit S256 method for PKCE authorization requests.
evidence.quote: Required an explicit S256 method for PKCE authorization requests

evidence.claim: The redirect_uri used in the code exchange must match the one used in the authorize step.
evidence.quote: Same redirect URI which you used in the previous step

evidence.claim: Redirect URIs must be absolute HTTP or HTTPS URLs, and an app can register 1 to 32 of them.
evidence.quote: Format: absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL

open_questions: The live creation form was not checked because it sits behind a login. It may also ask for a privacy policy URL, logo or description.
No source confirms whether Linear reviews public apps before other workspaces can install them. The docs mention no such review.
Linear publishes no review timeline for the Integration Directory.
A live PKCE exchange was not tested. The docs say client_secret is optional under PKCE.
Composio's guide lists 'admin' as a default scope but its toolkit catalog does not. Check your actual auth config.
The App authentication page with the full list of agent scopes (app:assignable, app:mentionable) was not fetched.
It is unclear whether the 'enable refresh tokens' toggle mentioned by one community guide still exists, given that all apps moved to rotating refresh tokens in April 2026.
